evidence.claim: Governor Ernest Lister vetoed a proposal in 1913, but a crossing finally opened on June 15, 1927, improving travel between northeastern Washington and northern Idaho.
evidence.quote: A proposed bridge was vetoed by Governor Ernest Lister in 1913, but the project remained a local concern. A bridge near Newport eventually opened to traffic on June 15, 1927.

evidence.claim: Oldtown and Newport share a built-up area divided by a straight state boundary, with no natural barrier between them.
evidence.quote: There are no natural or physical barriers, and it is strictly a political division, separated by the straight-line state boundary.

evidence.claim: The Idaho settlement was once called Newport, Idaho, and served as a port and supply point for the Pend Oreille Valley.
evidence.quote: Before adopting its current name, the Idaho-side settlement was commonly referred to as “Newport, Idaho.” The community initially served as a port and supply point for settlers in the Pend Oreille Valley

evidence.claim: As settlement expanded on the Washington side, the post office moved there and the Idaho settlement declined.
evidence.quote: As settlement expanded on the Washington side, the post office was moved there, and the original Idaho settlement gradually declined.

evidence.claim: It incorporated as Oldtown in April 1947.
evidence.quote: In April 1947, the former settlement was incorporated under the name Oldtown.

evidence.claim: The river and state line leave its main business district along US 2 just 700 feet of space on the Idaho side.
evidence.quote: Oldtown is squeezed between this boundary to the west and the river to the east, leaving the main business district on U.S. Route 2 with only 700 feet (210 meters) of space in which to operate on the Idaho side.

evidence.claim: Albeni Falls Dam occupies the site of a natural waterfall on the Pend Oreille River between Oldtown and Priest River.
evidence.quote: It is located on the site of a natural waterfall named Albeni Falls

evidence.claim: The falls were named for Albeni Poirier, a French immigrant who settled here in 1887.
evidence.quote: Albeni Falls was named after Albeni Poirier, a French immigrant who settled in the area in 1887.

evidence.claim: The Army Corps of Engineers began construction in 1951 to control flooding and supply electricity to the growing Pacific Northwest.
evidence.quote: Construction of the dam on the site of the original falls began during 1951 by the Army Corps of Engineers to control flooding and provide needed electricity to the growing Pacific Northwest.

evidence.claim: Completed in 1955, the dam is 90 feet high and 775 feet long, including a 400-foot spillway.
evidence.quote: The dam is 90 feet (27 m) high and 775 feet (236 m) long. Its spillway is 400 feet (120 m) long.

evidence.claim: Completed in 1955
evidence.quote: Construction on the dam began in 1951 and was completed in 1955

evidence.claim: More than 50 buildings traveled upriver on barges when A.C. White moved its mill town from Laclede to Dover.
evidence.quote: A.C. White relocated the entire Laclede mill town to Dover. With no more than winches and horses, more than 50 buildings were placed on barges and moved up river.

evidence.claim: The company bought Dover Lumber Company in 1922 after its Laclede mill burned, then moved the buildings with horses and winches.
evidence.quote: Dover dates back to 1922 when the A.C. White Lumber Company purchased the Dover Lumber Company after its mill in Laclede burned.

evidence.claim: One relocated building became Dover Church.
evidence.quote: Like many other houses, it was moved by barge on the Pend Oreille River to Dover in 1923

evidence.claim: Designed as a summer cottage for the White family, it was unfinished when the mill burned.
evidence.quote: It was built as a summer cottage in Laclede for lumber businessman A.C. White and his family, but it was not completed before the A.C. White lumber mill and factory in Laclede burned.

evidence.claim: Its eventual use as a church gave a rustic domestic design a different purpose.
evidence.quote: It became a church, and is unusual as a church for its rustic style.
